results.name: Open Season on Kapibala: Attacker Steals Over 18,000 Government Records Through WordPress Exploitation
results.description: A suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor, operating from UTC+8 timezone and linked to Red Heron, conducted extensive exploitation campaigns from May through September 2026. The adversary maintained persistent use of a single IP address to target multiple technologies including WordPress, ZyXEL switches, and various enterprise platforms. In the most severe incident, the attacker exploited WordPress vulnerabilities CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137 to breach a western government organization, stealing over 18,000 sensitive records containing credentials and personally identifiable information. Additionally, the actor exploited CVE-2026-7273 in ZyXEL GS1900 switches, compromising 996 devices across 48 countries and exfiltrating configurations and credentials. The attacker demonstrated sophisticated capabilities including custom tool development possibly leveraging large language models, privilege escalation attempts, and systematic data exfiltration using PowerShell-based collection and staging techniques.

results.name: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
results.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered PHP2Shell exploitation attempts in MadPot honeypot telemetry on October 17, 2026, four days before the public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The initial exploit originated from a commercial anonymization network, suggesting threat actor involvement during the embargo period. Multiple proof-of-concept exploits emerged on the disclosure date, with varied payloads and infrastructure indicating multiple actors. Following the embargo lift on October 21, 2026, exploitation became widespread within hours. This incident highlights two critical lessons: coordinated disclosure cannot guarantee zero-day protection, and AI-assisted analysis has dramatically shortened the time from patch release to working exploits, requiring organizations to measure patch timelines in hours rather than days.

results.name: New BlackX UEFI bootkit exploiting Baton Drop
results.description: In early 2026, a sophisticated APT campaign targeting diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan deployed BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to the notorious BlackLotus. The bootkit exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass Secure Boot and install malicious drivers into the Windows kernel. Despite patches being available since 2023, victims remained vulnerable because the mitigation requires manual activation by administrators. The campaign deploys cyberespionage payloads including a RAT using cloud storage for command and control, and OxiDLLRunner, a Rust-based payload. The attack demonstrates APT actors borrowing techniques from cybercrime operations, as BlackX appears to be reverse-engineered from BlackLotus code. Attribution points to APT41 based on code similarities and tactics matching previous campaigns.

results.name: LiteLLM PyPI Package and Docker Images Compromised to Steal Cloud and AI Credentials
results.description: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised through a supply chain attack affecting both PyPI packages and Docker images. The malicious release contains Python startup files that automatically execute upon Python initialization, stealing cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, and AI development tool authentication. Socket's AI scanner detected the compromise seven minutes after publication. Container build provenance reveals the attack used a lookalike repository (Berri-AI/litellm instead of BerriAI/litellm) in the release workflow. The payload targets AWS, Azure, Google Cloud credentials, GitHub CLI, SSH keys, npm/PyPI configuration, and AI tool credentials including Claude, Gemini, and Cursor. Stolen data is encrypted and exfiltrated to a command-and-control server. A separate loader mechanism enables remote Python code execution. The package receives approximately 23 million weekly downloads, making the impact significant.

results.name: PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
results.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, collectively named PHP2Shell, were disclosed on October 21, 2026. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory handling corruption that can interrupt PHP while internal request data is partially initialized, leading to invalid data treatment. CVE-2026-109619 exploits stale global state where request-owned internal state survives after memory is freed. Both vulnerabilities can be exploited successfully on ARM64 systems and x86 systems without ASLR. Fixed versions include PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Over 2.6 million internet-facing hosts running PHP were identified as vulnerable, with 42% on end-of-life branches receiving no official patches. Early exploitation attempts were observed from multiple sources, including scanning activity and webshell deployment attempts targeting the upload-progress vulnerability path.

results.name: INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware: Exposed AI Infrastructure
results.description: Threat researchers discovered an AI-driven intrusion ecosystem operated by affiliates of INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen Ransomware groups through seven exposed command-and-control servers. The operators integrated commercial AI models via OpenCode and OpenRouter, logging over 8,000 messages across 133 sessions with recorded spending exceeding $23,000. They exploited edge devices at scale including FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, and cPanel systems, compromising thousands of targets. The infrastructure contained 46 custom INC encryptor builds staged for October 1, 2026 deployment, evidence of live victim encryption, and a custom arsenal including the Phantom autonomous framework, Ghost C2, and various exploitation tools. The campaign targeted 62 named organizations, predominantly in the United States, with focus on industrial manufacturing and healthcare sectors. OPSEC failures in late September 2026 exposed source code, credentials, AI session logs, and complete victim knowledge bases.

results.name: Stray Cat, Open Doors: How k0t Wanders Through the Network Edge
results.description: Group-IB and NyxLab uncovered a large-scale campaign by threat actor k0t exploiting FortiGate, FortiWeb, and Palo Alto GlobalProtect edge devices to harvest credentials and establish persistent access. The operation involves exploiting CVE-2025-64446 in FortiWeb and CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect, alongside brute-forcing attacks using custom tools. Over 70,000 exposed credentials were discovered, with victims spanning multiple industries globally. Post-compromise activities include credential theft, Active Directory enumeration, and data exfiltration via Rclone to cloud storage. Persistence is maintained through MeshCentral, AdaptixC2, and various RMM tools including Atera and AnyDesk. The campaign shows overlaps with Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware groups, suggesting k0t may operate as an Initial Access Broker, though direct affiliation remains unconfirmed.

results.name: Amazon-Themed ClickFix Campaign Serves Up Finger-Licking Malware
results.description: Attackers leveraged a sponsored Google search result for 'amazon business' to redirect victims to a spoofed Amazon login page hosted on Google Sites. The page presented a fake CAPTCHA (ClickFix) that tricked users into executing a malicious command using Windows' finger utility, an obsolete network tool repurposed as a living-off-the-land binary. This initiated a complex infection chain downloading IronPython, executing obfuscated Python scripts, and deploying multiple payloads including Doina malware, Lumma Stealer via a Node.js package, and a pirated NetSupport Client RMM tool. The attack infrastructure predominantly used barbecue-themed domains for command and control. The campaign affected multiple organizations and demonstrates cross-platform capabilities, with alternate payloads prepared for macOS users. Attackers employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including Base64 encoding with Cyrillic character substitution, XOR encryption, and RC4 decryption throughout the infection stages.

results.name: "Next Exploit Opportunities": How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
results.description: A financially motivated threat actor operating under the handle BUGSTER leveraged jailbroken AI assistants, specifically the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4, to conduct multiple cybercrime operations across India. The actor, demonstrating limited technical skills but relying heavily on AI-generated scripts and reconnaissance, successfully exfiltrated over 5,200 personal records from a university database, conducted WordPress brute force attacks, and planned VoIP telecommunications fraud. Additional activities included Wi-Fi password cracking requiring physical proximity to targets, cryptocurrency whale reconnaissance, and development of credential scanning toolkits. The actor configured specialized AI bot profiles providing step-by-step criminal guidance, including fraud traffic ratios and carrier evasion techniques, demonstrating how AI lowers the skill barrier for cybercrime operations.

results.name: The Science of Exploitability: Decoding BlueHammer
results.description: BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) is an eight-stage local privilege-escalation chain targeting Windows Defender Antimalware Platform before version 4.18.26030.3011. It requires initial code execution as a standard user and chains CloudFilter callbacks, batch oplocks, object-manager symlinks, Defender's update RPC, offline SAM parsing, and SAMR operations to achieve NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM access. The exploit leverages legitimate Windows mechanisms rather than memory corruption, freezing MsMpEng.exe through CloudFilter manipulation while staging malicious update files. In laboratory testing, it successfully escalated privileges, recovered domain-admin credentials from LSASS, and enabled lateral movement via pass-the-hash to compromise domain controllers. Runtime factors including pending signature updates, WinDefend state, filter drivers, VSS, and CloudFilter reachability determine actual exploitability beyond version-based detection.
